Container.Name: print-handy

Branch.TagDescription: Stable. Moves only when a new Print Handy release is published. Recommended for a printer you rely on.
Development build, rebuilt nightly from main after the full CI suite passes. Features may be unfinished and settings may change without a release note.

Container.Overview: Share a model link or file in Discord, Telegram or Matrix. Choose filament, review the estimate and approve the exact job before it reaches your printer. Runs locally with no Print Handy cloud; chat providers carry what you send, and model downloads or optional hosted AI use the network. Camera monitoring and AI features are optional. A camera alert is not proof that a print is safe unattended. See the printer support guide for supported connection paths and hardware verification limits. Not affiliated with Bambu Lab. Full setup and upgrade instructions are in the Print Handy docs.
Container.ExtraParams: --user 1000:1000 --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges:true --shm-size 256m --log-driver json-file --log-opt max-size=10m --log-opt max-file=3 --restart unless-stopped --health-cmd "python3 /usr/local/bin/print-handy-healthcheck" --health-interval 30s --health-timeout 10s --health-start-period 90s --health-retries 3
Container.Requires: Appdata paths owned by UID/GID 1000. Existing Spoolman data can be copied into the Spoolman Data path before first start; nothing is migrated automatically.

Config.Name: State
Config.Description: Runtime state, prompts, hardware and job records, plus daily app logs in logs/ (kept 14 days, survive container recreate) and stop captures in state/stops/. Back this up. This is the state volume's neutral name since 2.2.5; before that it was /data/hermes — an existing install does not need to rename anything (see the legacy State path below and docs/DOCKER.md).

Config.Name: Archive
Config.Description: Sliced jobs and G-code. Back this up.

Config.Name: Records
Config.Description: Print records. Back this up.

Config.Name: Cache
Config.Description: Regenerable cache.

Config.Name: Spoolman data
Config.Description: Bundled Spoolman database, config, logs and backups. Back this up.

Config.Name: Account tokens
Config.Description: OPTIONAL. Account tokens for model sites (MakerWorld, Thingiverse and others), kept outside the container so they survive recreation. Create the folder and make it owned by 1000:1000 first; see docs/DOCKER.md.

Config.Name: Timelapse archive
Config.Description: Finished in-container timelapses are copied here (the code default archive directory). Point it at a media share if you keep timelapses there.

Config.Name: Web UI port
Config.Description: Container port of the Web UI, so the WebUI link works (PRINT_HANDY__WEBUI__PORT must match this port). While the Web UI is disabled below, nothing answers on it.

Config.Name: Spoolman port
Config.Description: OPTIONAL, LAN only (#443): publishes the bundled Spoolman API (container port 8000) so Moonraker on printer hardware (for example a ZMod AD5X) and Home Assistant can reach it at http://[unraid-ip]:7912. Leave this mapping deleted to keep Spoolman loopback-only inside the container. Publishing it also requires SPOOLMAN_HOST=0.0.0.0 below, or Spoolman still refuses the connection. The API is unauthenticated: never forward this port from a router.

Config.Name: Settings file
Config.Description: Leave as is, or point at a mounted YAML file for list settings.

Config.Name: Bot mode
Config.Description: Must be standalone in Docker.

Config.Name: Discord bot token
Config.Description: Secret. Leave empty to stage the listener and Spoolman without the Discord bot.

Config.Name: Discord channel ID
Config.Description: Channel Print Handy uses.

Config.Name: Allowed user IDs
Config.Description: Optional whitelist of Discord user IDs allowed to use the bot, comma or space separated. Leave empty (the default) and everyone who can post in the print channel can use the bot — the channel is the access boundary.

Config.Name: Discord approval user ID
Config.Description: Discord user ID allowed to approve prints; always allowed to use the bot as well. Empty leaves approvals to the allowed users (or, with no whitelist, the channel).

Config.Name: Discord timezone
Config.Description: IANA timezone for display times and the daily session reset, for example America/New_York. Separate from the container timezone below.

Config.Name: Printer model
Config.Description: flashforge.ad5x, flashforge.ad5m, flashforge.ad5m_pro, flashforge.creator5, flashforge.creator5_pro, sovol.sv06, klipper.generic, octoprint.marlin, bambulab.a1 or bambulab.p1s (Bambu Lab models are offline only).

Config.Name: Moonraker URL
Config.Description: Klipper printers, for example http://printer.example:7125. Fluidd is not needed here.

Config.Name: Spoolman URL
Config.Description: Bundled Spoolman API by default. To use an existing external Spoolman, set its URL here and set Bundled Spoolman to false; nothing is migrated.

Config.Name: Bundled Spoolman
Config.Description: true runs the bundled Spoolman API; false uses the external Spoolman URL.

Config.Name: Spoolman CORS origin
Config.Description: Optional (#798): exact browser origin allowed to call the bundled Spoolman, for Fluidd/Mainsail live updates, for example http://PRINTER-IP. Scheme and port are part of the match; a bare IP:port never matches. Leave empty to keep CORS off. Never use *.

Config.Name: Spoolman bind host
Config.Description: Host the bundled Spoolman API binds to inside the container (#443). Default 127.0.0.1 keeps it loopback-only and unexposed, even with the Spoolman port mapping above present. Set 0.0.0.0 ONLY when you publish the Spoolman port for LAN Moonraker (printer hardware) or Home Assistant access; the API is unauthenticated, so keep it on the LAN and never forward it from a router.

Config.Name: Camera watch
Config.Description: Camera watchdog: posts a Discord photo alert for spaghetti, a detached part, an empty bed or a stalled print. Alert only; it never controls the printer. Needs a camera snapshot and a vision endpoint (see docs/DOCKER.md). This variable is an environment override: Unraid always passes it, so it wins over visual_watch.enabled in a mounted config file; change it here.

Config.Name: Camera watch sensitivity
Config.Description: How readily the camera watchdog alerts, 1 (quietest) to 5 (most alerts). 3 is the original behavior; periodic checks run every 30, 20, 15, 10 or 7.5 minutes for levels 1 to 5. This variable is an environment override: Unraid always passes it, so it wins over visual_watch.sensitivity in a mounted config file; change it here.

Config.Name: Camera watch early layers
Config.Description: Early-layer camera watch (#913): a risky print (slicer finding, print anyway override, supports decision) is checked on every layer change for this many first layers. Normal prints are unchanged. This variable is an environment override: Unraid always passes it, so it wins over visual_watch.early_layers in a mounted config file; change it here.

Config.Name: Camera watch early interval
Config.Description: Seconds between camera checks of a risky print during its early layers, even when no layer changes. This variable is an environment override: Unraid always passes it, so it wins over visual_watch.early_interval_s in a mounted config file; change it here.

Config.Name: Camera watch auto-pause
Config.Description: THIS PAUSES THE PRINTER. When true, two suspicious camera verdicts in a row (spaghetti, detached or air) during a risky print's early layers send PAUSE through the alert pause path. It never cancels; the alert keeps its stop and resume buttons. Off by default. This variable is an environment override: Unraid always passes it, so it wins over visual_watch.auto_pause_early in a mounted config file; change it here.

Config.Name: Vision chat URL
Config.Description: OpenAI-compatible endpoint for camera checks and roasts. Empty disables both; set it together with the vision API key below.

Config.Name: Timelapse capture
Config.Description: In-container timelapse capture (#246): starts the bundled go2rtc to normalise the camera source on loopback. Off by default and opt-in; off keeps the printer-rendered timelapse behaviour. This variable is an environment override: when set it wins over timelapse.capture_enabled in a mounted config file. Capture needs a camera source for your printer family (a Moonraker webcam, Bambu stills or X1 RTSPS stream, a PrusaLink-registered camera, or an AD5X accessory camera; Elegoo SDCP has no verified camera source yet — see docs/DOCKER.md). Separate from the SSH timelapse archive (timelapse.archive_host / archive_dir in the config file): in-container capture never uses it, but printer-rendered videos are delivered only through it — with archive_host/archive_dir unset, the printer-rendered lookup is skipped and no rendered video is attached. go2rtc's API/RTSP stay on loopback and are never published.

Config.Name: Timelapse capture trigger
Config.Description: Stage 2 frame capture trigger (#246): interval (a frame every capture interval), layer (a frame on each layer change), or both.

Config.Name: Timelapse capture interval (s)
Config.Description: Seconds between captured frames for the interval trigger (#246 stage 2).

Config.Name: Timelapse capture max frames
Config.Description: Per-job cap on captured frames (#246 stage 2); 0 disables the cap.

Config.Name: Timelapse capture max bytes
Config.Description: Per-job cap on captured frame bytes (#246 stage 2); 0 disables the cap.

Config.Name: Timelapse capture encoder
Config.Description: Encoder preference for the Stage 3 timelapse encode (#246): auto, vaapi, nvenc, qsv or cpu. Capture itself never encodes.

Config.Name: Vision model
Config.Description: Model the vision endpoint uses for camera checks.

Config.Name: Roast
Config.Description: The one-line roast added to print-started and print-complete posts. On by default: it runs whenever an LLM/vision endpoint is available (the vision chat URL and API key above), on every platform, Telegram included. Set false to turn roasts off; camera checks keep working either way.

Config.Name: Vision API key
Config.Description: Secret. Key for the vision chat URL above.

Config.Name: Hermes agent API key
Config.Description: Secret. Key for the [agent] stray-chat lane: scoped to the Hermes 3dprinting profile only (/p/3dprinting/), which is locked to web-only tools. The lane endpoint itself (agent.chat_url) is set in the config file.

Config.Name: Discord chat LLM
Config.Description: Free-text chat replies from the LLM below on Discord. On by default. Set false to run Discord as a pure bot: unmatched text gets the short not-understood reply, while the LLM stays configured for /print-design (which inherits it). Roasts and camera checks keep their own vision settings either way.

Config.Name: Web UI
Config.Description: Web UI (#286, #440): a simple status page plus picker configuration that syncs to the YAML settings file. On by default so the WebUI link works. With the access token below empty, the first visit shows a setup page where you set a password or confirm you want it open on your LAN; nothing else is served until you choose. Set false to turn it off entirely; then nothing listens and the Web UI port above answers nothing.

Config.Name: Web UI bind host
Config.Description: Host the Web UI binds to inside the container. The template default 0.0.0.0 makes it reachable through the Web UI port mapping. Use 127.0.0.1 to keep it inside the container.

Config.Name: Web UI port setting
Config.Description: Port the Web UI listens on inside the container; must match the Web UI port mapping above. 0 disables the listener even when the Web UI is enabled.

Config.Name: Web UI access token
Config.Description: Secret, optional. Empty: the Web UI's first-run setup page asks you to set a password or leave it open. Set a long random value to use a token instead (it overrides the setup choice): the WebUI link then opens the login page, where you paste it once to get a browser session; API clients (the Home Assistant integration) send it, or the setup password, as the X-WebUI-Token header. Never a setting in a config file.

Config.Name: Container timezone
Config.Description: IANA timezone for the container's local time — log timestamps, scheduled and timed features and the bundled services' timestamps — for example Europe/London. The image default is America/New_York; an unknown name is logged at startup and the default is used. Separate from the Discord display timezone above.
